title: Member Services Training Notes: Prepaid Dental HMO Plans Enrollments per Covered Person
content:
**Rule.** Under the Prepaid Dental HMO Plans, a subscriber may hold one DHMO enrollment per covered person, with no fixed cap per subscriber; a person may not have a second applied or active Cascade DHMO enrollment. Each covered person has an own primary care dentist assignment; family members may be assigned to different dentists.

The rule has three parts, each answered below.

**1. How many DHMO enrollments may one subscriber hold?**
One for each covered person. There is no fixed cap on the number of enrollments per subscriber; the count follows the number of covered persons.

**2. May the same person be enrolled twice?**
No. A person may not have a second Cascade DHMO enrollment that is applied or active. The test is the person, not the subscriber: a person with an applied enrollment, or with an active enrollment, may not have another applied or active one.

| The person already holds a Cascade DHMO enrollment that is… | A second applied or active Cascade DHMO enrollment for that person |
|---|---|
| applied | Not permitted |
| active | Not permitted |

**3. Does every covered person have the same dentist?**
Not necessarily. Each covered person has an own primary care dentist assignment, and family members may be assigned to different dentists.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A subscriber covers a spouse and three children under the Prepaid Dental HMO Plans. The household holds five DHMO enrollments, one per covered person, and that number is permitted because there is no fixed cap per subscriber. The spouse may be assigned to one primary care dentist and the children to another; each of the five has an own assignment.
